rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2013> the authors ran their own NFT hydroponic lettuce experiment with six treatments (control, DBD plasma, nanocavitation, hybrid 3/9/15 min), five plants per treatment, 35-day cycle, measuring leaf number, fresh and dry weights, colour, flavonoid, K and Fe.
rows.notes: The study does report, as its own result (Results, Figs. 4<U+2013>11), a 59 % increase in shoot fresh weight and 58 % in shoot dry matter of lettuce for the 9-min plasma-nanobubble hybrid treatment versus control, which is the ~60 % figure quoted in the passage. However, the system is a nutrient-film-technique hydroponic channel, not drip irrigation; the claim row is filed under technology 'drip', and the study contains no drip-irrigation treatment, so Q2 is answered 'no' on technology grounds and technology_mismatch is flagged. For reference had the technology matched: single method (plant harvest measurements, no triangulation); no intermediate variable (dissolved oxygen, nitrate, RONS in the solution) was measured, only hypothesised; one crop, one hydroponic unit, no multi-site evaluation; no scale above the bench-top unit; authors state limitations on generalizability (plants, nutrient solutions, plasma method, gas flow) and small sample size in the Discussion; results given as Duncan letter groupings with no SD/SE/CI reported in the text.

notes: Full text appears complete (Introduction through Conclusion), but figures and tables are not reproduced, so any error bars in Figs. 4<U+2013>11 cannot be verified. The study is a small feasibility trial (5 plants per treatment, one lettuce cultivar, one NFT system) funded by the company developing the technology.
